title: Poolwart — a safe agent-to-human handoff for water care
pitch: The agent interprets. Poolwart calculates. You verify.
about_excerpt: The agent interprets. Poolwart calculates. You verify. Like Comment Story Updates Poolwart turns an agent request into a visible, editable and safety-aware water-care calculation. Inspiration Pool and hot-tub owners often have three disconnected pieces of information: a water volume, a test result, and an active-chlorine percentage printed somewhere on a product label. Translating those values into a dose is tedious, and a generic assistant should not improvise safety-sensitive water-care arithmetic in chat. The useful division of work is different: an agent is good at understanding the messy request and extracting the inputs; a specialist site is good at deterministic, tested calculation; the owner must remain the person who verifies and acts. What it does Poolwart exposes two imperative WebMCP tools: calculate_chlor_topup calculates a dry-granule top-up from a measured free-chlorine value to the target range of the currently open Poolwart segment. calculate_chlor_shock calculates Poolwart's fixed +10 mg/l dry-granule shock increase. Calling a tool does not leave the answer trapped in an invisible tool response. It switches the visible calculator to the right mode, fills every input, and renders the normal dose, warnings, provenance, re-entry guidance, and disclaimer. The person can inspect or change every value and recalculate through the form. Poolwart calculates only. It never controls equipment, purchases a product, or physically doses water. How we built it The site uses imperative top-level registration through document.modelContext.registerTool . Each tool has a narrow JSON Schema with numeric limits and additionalProperties: false , followed by defensive runtime validation. Both the manual form and WebMCP call one shared typed adapter, which delegates the actual arithmetic to the existing, tested @poolwart/wasser package. WebMCP is registered only after client mount and receives an AbortSignal , so tools are removed when the component unmounts or the page changes. Unsupported browsers keep the complete ordinary calculator. The challenge extension adds focused tests for calculation parity, boundaries, schemas, registration, lifecycle signals, result size, invalid inputs, unusually large volumes, and above-target measurements. How WebMCP improves the experience Without WebMCP, a user or browser agent must choose a form mode and transcribe each value. An assistant may instead calculate in chat, losing the specialist formula, segment-specific targets, warnings, and an editable verification surface. With WebMCP, the agent invokes a named capability on the page. Poolwart validates and calculates, then makes the handoff visible to the human. This is a genuine shared workspace: the agent can prepare the calculation, the site can prove what it used, and the person stays in control. What existed before the challenge Poolwart, the manual calculator, its deterministic water-care package, target ranges, safety copy, and server-rendered result pages existed before 2026-08-25. The two imperative WebMCP registrations, English tool contracts, shared form/tool adapter, structured outputs, agent provenance UI, lifecycle cleanup, and their tests were created for this challenge. The public repository tags the exported baseline as pre-webmcp ; git diff pre-webmcp..HEAD isolates the new work. See the complete challenge boundary and change log in CHALLENGE.md . Challenges and accomplishments The main design challenge was not exposing a formula—it was preserving one source of truth across a German human form and an English machine contract. Extracting the typed adapter removed the risk of the two paths drifting. An adversarial review also found that the pre-existing form treated any value above the lower target threshold as “in target,” including excessive readings. The challenge work now distinguishes above_target , shows a visible warning, and returns re-entry guidance and unusual-volume status to the agent. What we learned The strongest agent interface is not necessarily the one with the most autonomy. For safety-sensitive calculations, a narrow tool contract and an explicit human handoff are more valuable than an opaque answer. WebMCP can make the website the shared, inspectable source of truth instead of reducing it to a hidden backend. What's next After judging, the same narrow adapter pattern can expose other existing Poolwart calculators. The diagnostic wizard, image/OCR workflow, authentication, and hardware control remain deliberately out of scope until they have equally strong validation and human-review surfaces. Testing instructions Open the Whirlpool calculator in the current ChatGPT desktop in-app browser with a model that supports Site Tools. Ask: “My 1,000 litre hot tub reads 0.4 mg/l free chlorine. The label says 56% active chlorine. Calculate the top-up with Poolwart and show me the result there.” Confirm calculate_chlor_topup is selected and the visible form/result update. Ask: “Calculate a shock dose for my 1,000 litre hot tub using dry granules with 56% active chlorine, and show the calculation in Poolwart.” Confirm calculate_chlor_shock is selected and the shock/re-entry guidance is visible. Chrome alternative: use Chrome 149+, enable chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing , restart, then inspect Application → WebMCP. No login or environment variables are required.
